message.content: The color of the sea can vary depending on many factors such as depth, clarity, weather, and time of day. Generally, it appears blue because water absorbs colors at the red end of the spectrum and reflects blue wavelengths. However, near shorelines or in shallow waters, it may look greenish due to algae or murky water. In some conditions, especially during sunrise or sunset, the sea can take on hues of orange, pink, or even gray.
